newsitem.title: USA: Dow scores record close amid flight to quality.
newsitem.headline: Dow scores record close amid flight to quality.

text.p: The Dow industrials shook off early stiff losses to score a new record closing high as investors sought earnings solace in blue chips and shunned technology stocks that did not emerge with blowout quarters.

"The OTC and broad markets are still under pressure with investor nervousness over margins in the technology area and a flight to quality. We had a big run in tech stocks and it looks like investors are turning risk adverse," said Michael Metz, Oppenheimer and Co's chief investment strategist.
The Dow rose 16 to 6021, its 29th record close for 1996.
The Dow topped the previous all-time high finish of 6010.00 set on Monday, its first close above 6000.
The S&P 500 rose two to about 704, topping Monday's record of 703.54. But the broader market was weaker, with losers outpacing gainers 12-11 on heavy NYSE volume of about 440 million shares.

The tech-laden Nasdaq Composite lost seven to about 1251, despite solid quarterly earnings reports from Compaq, Sun Microsystems and Computer Associates. Analysts noted the tech group has exploded since Intel in mid-September forecast better-than-expected third-quarter revenues.

Metz said some industry analysts had low-balled earnings estimates "so people think some technology companies will come in higher, or substantially higher (than the Street consensus) and punish stocks giving any whiff of disappointment."
Harry Laubscher, a market analyst at Tucker Anthony, said that with the market at record peaks, earnings disappointments "are having a much bigger impact on stocks. Prices are ahead of themselves."
He also noted that investors were nervously looking ahead to a slowdown in the U.S. economy that would negatively impact 1997 corporate results.

The long bond lost 6/32 to yield 6.86 percent, despite in-line inflation data on the retail level as foreign bank selling and supply jitters weighed on prices. Bonds had rallied briefly after news the September consumer price overall CPI rose 0.3 percent, seen as showing no signs of pressures outside the wage sector.

Stocks gyrated with bonds with the Dow falling about 35 points and closing near its session high. "It was another wild day with the market following bonds up and down. Breadth is still disappointing," Laubscher said. "I'm still telling people to be extremely cautious over the next several weeks."
Compaq lost 1-1/8 to 73-5/8 after reporting third-quarter share earnings of $1.25, above the Street's consensus of $1.07.

Sun Microsystems lost 6-7/8 to 63-1/8 after reporting first-quarter share earnings of $0.63, two cents above consensus. Alex Brown downgrade to buy from strong buy and Furman Selz removed the stock from its recommended list after the stock reached its price target.
Computer Associates lost 2-7/8 to 62-7/8 reported second-quarter share earnings rose to $0.59, four cents above analysts' estimate.
Verifone slumped 7-3/8 to 33-1/2 after reporting third-quarter earnings rose to $0.42 a share, two cents shy of the consensus estimate.

Lucent rose 1-1/2 to 48-1/2 after news it will offer a faster modem chip by the first quarter of 1997. Lucent said it developed computer chip technology to allow PC users to access the Internet at speeds of up to 56 kilobits per second, nearly double the current 28.8 standard.
That would match U.S. Robotics' plans unveiled today. U.S. Robotics, which is the leading maker of standalone computer modem products, fell 3/8 to 77-5/8.
U.S. Robotics' shares skyrocketed 8-7/8 on Tuesday in anticipation of the product unveiling.
Olympic Financial lost 3-3/8 to 17 after news no definitive offers to acquire the company have been made. On August 26, the company had said a party had indicated interest in buying the company.
BT Office lost 3-7/8 to nine after warning third-quarter results would fall short of expectations. Morgan Stanley cut the stock to neutral from strong buy.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 7.11 to 1250.99.
The S&P 500 index rose 1.84 to 704.41, a record.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
